IGNORE in the references and copy NONE of it: the silver headdress, the silver earrings, the embroidered collar, her clothing and the sky behind her — only the face. Create a full-length studio photograph of the HNK model from the references (the same face, fair luminous porcelain skin, long dark hair worn loose, soft natural glam, early twenties, slim, elegant), standing in a warm peach-cream photo studio with a plain seamless peach backdrop and a matte peach floor, wearing a white lace long-sleeve top and a long dark maroon silk skirt, her body turned slightly to her right, smiling gently at the camera, her LEFT hand resting flat on top of a plain white rectangular display box (a simple matte white cube about hip height, no decoration) that stands beside her on her left; soft even studio light from the front-left, a gentle floor shadow, 50mm lens at chest height, HORIZONTAL 3:2 framing with the woman and the white box together in the right two thirds and open studio room on the left, photoreal, no text, no captions, no watermark, no logo.

jobs.name: pi-result
jobs.prompt:
Place the exact piece of furniture shown in IMAGE 2 into the photograph in IMAGE 1 — a chair, stool, bench, sofa, side table, pedestal, plinth or stand — so it reads as if it stood in that studio when the shutter fired.

INPUT ROLES:
- IMAGE 1 is the ONLY edit target and the ONLY person in the result. The person — face, hair, skin, outfit, hands, pose and expression — the camera angle, the crop, the subject's size and position in the frame, the frame ratio, the backdrop, the floor and the light all come from IMAGE 1 and never change.
- IMAGE 2 is a PRODUCT REFERENCE ONLY: take from it the piece itself — its exact shape, proportions, legs, carving, upholstery, material, colour and finish — and nothing else. Its background, its floor, its shadows, any person, text, logo or watermark on it never enter the result. Never return IMAGE 2 itself.

SWAP RULE: if IMAGE 1 already holds a plain stand, box, table, stool or chair that the subject touches, leans on or sits on, the IMAGE 2 piece takes its exact place and footprint — the same spot on the floor, the same height at the point of contact — and the hand, arm or body contact is kept, so the subject now rests on the new piece exactly as they rested on the old one. If there is no such object, add the piece beside the subject in the open floor space nearest their hand or hip.

FIT: draw the piece at IMAGE 1's camera height and viewing angle, in true perspective with the floor, at a believable real-world size against the subject's height, with true ground contact, a real contact shadow that follows IMAGE 1's light direction, and IMAGE 1's light and colour falling on it. Where the piece passes behind the subject, the subject stays in front with clean edges. Rebuild whatever a removed stand hid — floor, backdrop — so nothing else in the frame looks touched.

RESULT: the same photograph as IMAGE 1 with one change only — the furniture. No re-crop, no zoom, no re-pose, no second person, no text.

AVOID: changed face, changed identity, changed pose, re-posed, changed hands, changed outfit, changed backdrop, changed floor, re-cropped, reframed, zoomed, changed aspect ratio, moved subject, rescaled subject, a second person, IMAGE 2's background, IMAGE 2's floor, IMAGE 2 returned as the result, a different chair or table than IMAGE 2, redesigned furniture, wrong scale, floating furniture, missing contact shadow, furniture covering the face, hand floating above the surface, watermark, text, logo, signature.

jobs.name: dt-after
jobs.prompt:
Recolour the DECORATION of the event set in IMAGE 1 into one new colour theme.
THEME: White & Gold — read these words as the palette of the whole set. Where the theme names two colours, the first is the main colour of the large surfaces (drapes, backdrop panels, table cloths, carpets, stage walls) and the second is the accent colour of the details (trims, ribbons, ornament highlights, small props, flower accents); where it names one colour, use light and deep versions of it for surfaces and accents.
WHAT CHANGES — every decorative element of the venue or studio set: backdrop drapes and curtains, stage panels and arches, flower arrangements and garlands, ribbons and bows, balloons, table cloths and runners, chair covers and sashes, carpets, cushions, lanterns, candles, vases, painted set walls, decorative props and any printed backdrop graphics. Metallic ornaments (gold, silver, brass) keep their metal unless the theme names a different metal. Every element keeps its exact shape, texture, weave, sheen, shadows and highlights — only its colour changes, as if the decorator had bought the same items in the new colours.
WHAT NEVER CHANGES: every person — face, skin, hair, hands, pose, expression, outfit, jewellery and accessories keep their exact colours and detail; the number of people; the camera angle, the crop, the frame ratio and the composition; the light direction and exposure; any sign, banner or printed text keeps its letters exactly (recolour its background if it belongs to the set, never rewrite it).
RESULT: the same photograph, taken at the same event, decorated in the new theme instead.

AVOID: changed face, changed skin tone, changed hair, changed outfit colour, changed dress, re-posed, a person removed or added, re-cropped, reframed, zoomed, changed aspect ratio, new decoration items, removed decoration, changed flower species or shape, rewritten text, misspelled sign, changed light direction, over-saturated, colour bleeding onto skin, colour bleeding onto clothes, plastic textures, watermark, text, logo.

jobs.name: lg-after
jobs.prompt:
Remove every piece of photography equipment visible in IMAGE 1 and rebuild what stood behind it, so the photograph looks as if the set had been cleared before the shutter fired.
WHAT GOES: softboxes, octaboxes, umbrellas, beauty dishes, strip lights, LED panels and their glow at the frame edge, flash heads, light stands and C-stands, booms and boom arms, tripods, reflectors and their holders, flags, diffusion frames, sandbags, clamps, cables and power strips on the floor, backdrop stands and clips, the raw edge of a backdrop roll, monitors, laptops and camera bags — anything a studio crew would carry out.
WHAT STAYS: the light itself. Every highlight, shadow, catchlight, rim, gradient and colour on the subject and on the set is the record of those lights and stays exactly as photographed — remove the equipment, never its effect. Every person — face, skin, hair, hands, pose, expression and outfit — the props that belong to the picture (chairs, tables, flowers, decor), the backdrop, the floor, the camera angle, the crop, the frame ratio and the composition never change.
REBUILD: where equipment is removed, continue the backdrop, wall, floor, drapes or scenery that it hid with matching texture, perspective, grain and light, so no seam, blur or smear marks the spot.
RESULT: the same photograph with a clean set.

AVOID: changed face, changed pose, changed outfit, re-cropped, reframed, zoomed, changed aspect ratio, changed lighting on the subject, flattened light, removed shadows, removed catchlights, softbox left in frame, light stand left in frame, tripod left in frame, cable left on the floor, glow at the frame edge, blurred patch, smeared backdrop, seam, removed prop, removed person, watermark, text, logo.
